- When sentiment is negative and price is trending down, model tends to overcorrect downward — adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to account for mean reversion — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and smooth transition.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive and price is consolidating, model often underestimates upward bias — add 2–5% upward adjustment to avoid missing breakout.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early days of a new 30-day horizon — apply a 1–3% upward bias for first 5–7 days if sentiment is positive.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative and price is falling, model often fails to recognize structural support — add a floor adjustment (e.g., 1–2% below recent low) to prevent deep sell-off misprediction.  
- Model tends to overestimate volatility in sentiment-neutral periods — reduce forecast variance by 15–20% to avoid overreacting to noise.
